_readme: Classified drift exceptions for the structural contract gate (Gate B).
Each rule matches drift paths by prefix; 'class' is one of:
compatibility-exception — canonical intentionally open (v0.x additive policy); the consumer's stricter closed-world model is allowed and MUST NOT force a canonical change.
intentional-extension   — the consumer models more structure than canonical v0.x specifies; canonical adoption is evaluated per field, not automatic.
reconcile               — the two sides model the same concept differently; needs a tracked reconciliation decision before the gate may fail on it.
New drift that matches no rule fails --strict. Removing a canonical field, or changing a shared enum, will not match any rule and will fail CI by design.

exceptions.reason: signature optionality: canonical keeps signature optional (v0.x additive contract); the consumer requires it and closes the world. Optionality alignment is tracked as the JS signed/unsigned record-type split; additionalProperties stays intentionally open canonically.
consumer narrows alg to const ed25519 (stricter is allowed) and does not yet model canonical-optional signature.bundle / transparency_log_ref.

consumer models richer per-action structure (capability_decision, permission_gate, argument_drift, side_effect_class, recording_mode, exit_code, outcome, delta_ref, state_digest_*) than canonical v0.x enumerates; canonical adoption evaluated per field.
consumer adds approval_mode / deny_reason_class / approval_extension to top-level capability decisions; canonical underspecified.
consumer closes budget sub-objects; canonical keeps them open. Sub-state itself matches (required spent/actual_ms on both sides).
consumer closes the record; canonical open. Required keys match.
consumer closes the record; canonical open. Required uri matches.
consumer closes the record; canonical open. Required uri matches.
consumer closes envelope/signature records; canonical open. Required keys match.
RFC-3161-style timestamp proof structure attached post-signing; modeled in consumer, not yet canonical.
chain linkage modeled in consumer; canonical adoption pending (chain verification semantics tracked in wasmagent-protocol#214).
consumer adds session_id / turn_index to run_context.

divergent modeling of argument drift: canonical models declared vs actual digests + drifted args + diff summary; the consumer models approved vs observed digests + resolution. Needs one reconciled model before either side changes.
placement divergence: canonical carries it run-level; the consumer carries it per-action. Same vocabulary, different layer.
